key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-mediated protection against environmental degradation.
engineering_relevance: The planar architecture offers a route to hybrid photovoltaics that integrate optical, charge-transport, and protective functions without substrate texturing.
method: Benchmark trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells on untextured substrates.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Evaluate graphene’s protective role through 75 days of ambient exposure.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 days, compared with approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75-day ambient stability; longer-term durability and scalable fabrication of defect-free graphene barriers remain unestablished.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
